theme: 3 terms on how an iOS app starts and runs: the static screen shown at startup, the object for app-wide events, and the object for one window's events

terms.definition: The static screen iOS shows while your app is starting, before your first real screen appears.
terms.example: Make the Launch Screen look like the first screen, so the start feels fast.
terms.code:
// Info.plist entry
let key = "UILaunchStoryboardName"
let file = "LaunchScreen"
print("\(key) = \(file)")

terms.definition: The object that receives app-wide events from iOS, like the moment launch finishes.
terms.example: Put the analytics setup in the App Delegate, it only needs to run once at launch.

terms.definition: The object that handles the events of one window of your app, like going to the background.
terms.example: The Scene Delegate saves the draft when the user leaves the app.

quizzes.question: In this code, which object does this method belong to?

video.description:
Learn to explain how an iOS app starts and runs: Launch Screen, App Delegate & Scene Delegate, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Launch Screen - The static screen iOS shows while your app is starting, before your first real screen appears.
App Delegate - The object that receives app-wide events from iOS, like the moment launch finishes.
Scene Delegate - The object that handles the events of one window of your app, like going to the background.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Launch Screen, App Delegate & Scene Delegate in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
런치 스크린, 앱 델리게이트, 씬 델리게이트 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Launch Screen - The static screen iOS shows while your app is starting, before your first real screen appears.
한국어: 런치 스크린: 앱이 시작되는 동안 첫 화면이 나오기 전에 iOS가 보여주는 정적인 화면

App Delegate - The object that receives app-wide events from iOS, like the moment launch finishes.
한국어: 앱 델리게이트: 실행이 끝나는 순간처럼 앱 전체에 관한 이벤트를 iOS로부터 받는 객체

Scene Delegate - The object that handles the events of one window of your app, like going to the background.
한국어: 씬 델리게이트: 백그라운드로 가는 것처럼 앱의 창 하나에 관한 이벤트를 처리하는 객체

landscape.hook: Your timer keeps running in the background. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why is the timer still running?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the workout `timer` kept running after I left the app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Our app uses scenes, so iOS never calls that one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then who gets the background event?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Scene Delegate. Move the pause into `sceneDidEnterBackground`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why the Scene Delegate and not the App Delegate?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Each window of the app is a scene. The App Delegate keeps launch and app setup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. Could I start the `timer` from the Launch Screen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, the Launch Screen is just a static picture. It runs none of our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Nothing runs on the Launch Screen, and the Scene Delegate pauses the `timer`.
The Launch Screen is just a picture, none of your code runs there.
